sourceScope: Storage package public API, JavaScript adapter, native backend wiring, and generated Nitro bindings
Storage Expo example routes, components, and smoke-test adapter fixtures
Storage agent-device flows and replay coverage manifest

suites.purpose: Assert public Storage values, the native secure backend capability, observer registration and cleanup, and bounded QA smoke cases
Assert native Disk and Secure public API results, migrations, transactions, query semantics, and QA-key cleanup
Assert a no-prompt native Secure roundtrip and report untested hardware prerequisites as pending
Assert deterministic Disk and Secure write/read counts and cleanup
Open the installed example E2E route and verify its public deep-link value
Seed one RUN_ID-scoped native Disk key, relaunch the app, verify its exact value, and delete that key

Assert item merge and setOrDelete, Set toggle, clearGroup, TTL expiry events, Secure inventory, access control, coalesced Secure writes, invalid keys, scoped metrics, native Disk events, hooks, auth-storage TTL, and a passcode access-control probe on reserved QA keys
Enroll simulator Face ID, seed one RUN_ID-scoped biometric Secure item, match the read prompt, delete it, and unenroll; iOS simulator only
Seed one reserved key per scope, call clearAll, and verify each is absent; this wipes all example storage and must run last

features.transport: The RenameFrom control migrates the QA Disk key and reports the exact migrated value.
A Memory StorageItem returns the value written through its public setter.
The public Secure async-write option is enabled, flushed, read back, and restored.
The audit control checks key registration, duplicate detection, and group membership before deleting its Memory item.
The typed Set item stores and returns the red member, then clears its QA value.
The default native entry reports its platform Secure backend and returns then deletes a QA Secure value without a biometric operation.
The public scheduled-flush error observer can be installed and cleared through the runtime boundary.
features.claimLimit: No backend failure is induced and no callback delivery is claimed by this deterministic replay.

features.transport: The bounded Memory loop reads back each of its 200 values and deletes every QA key.
The deterministic SmokeTestRunner reaches its completed state with no failed native cases.
features.claimLimit: Requires exactly 39 passing cases out of 41, zero failures, and the two expected web-only skips; a newly skipped native case fails replay. Hardware prerequisite rows remain separate.

features.transport: The public testing entrypoint runs one isolated registerMigration / migrateToLatest fixture and resets its in-memory module.
features.claimLimit: This checks migration behavior at the in-memory testing adapter boundary and does not claim native Disk persistence.

features.transport: A constructed tagged Error is classified through the react-native-nitro-storage/testing entrypoint.
features.claimLimit: This is a public testing-entry fixture only; it does not simulate a native backend failure or scheduled flush delivery.

features.transport: The smoke runner removes only its reserved __smoke_ keys from Memory, Disk, and Secure and verifies that prefix is empty.
The installed example opens its Integrity route and reports the route ready.
features.claimLimit: The ready row proves only that the Integrity screen mounted; it does not prove any Storage operation.

features.transport: The route marks the full required case list finished and reports zero failures and zero skipped cases.
features.claimLimit: The finished marker proves only that the sweep ended; each required case needs its own asserted result.

features.transport: The required Integrity cases finish with fail=0 and skip=0.
features.claimLimit: The summary reports zero recorded failures and skips; it does not replace the individual case assertions.

features.transport: Public Storage capabilities identify the native SQLite Disk and platform Secure backends.
Disk prefix lookup preserves case while namespace cleanup removes only the matching key.
Memory raw values preserve the reserved literal prefix and typed set membership supports prototype-named values.
Disk prefix queries treat wildcard, slash, Unicode, and NUL test prefixes as literals.
Disk and Secure raw values, keys, imports, and prefix queries preserve NUL and Unicode data.
A raw Disk value and a Disk StorageItem return their exact written strings.
A non-biometric Secure StorageItem returns its exact written value and is deleted after the check.
A raw Disk import is visible after flushDiskWrites().
A Disk transaction rollback preserves its committed value after the callback throws.
The public renameFrom migration moves the legacy value and removes its old Disk key.
A Disk item namespace and a namespaced raw key remain distinct from the unprefixed key.
Disk cache metrics record a miss, a hit, and a cached entry for one QA item.
A short-lived Disk StorageItem returns its default after expiry.
Secure setBatch and getBatch return the exact two values before both QA keys are removed.
A Secure transaction rollback preserves its committed value after the callback throws.
Disk prefix lookup returns the known keys and the targeted removal leaves the keep key value intact.
The Integrity route deletes only its reserved test prefixes and exact legacy QA keys, then confirms those prefixes are empty.
The installed example opens the Keychain lab route and reports the route ready.
features.claimLimit: The ready row proves only that the Keychain screen mounted; it does not prove Secure storage succeeded.

features.transport: The native platform Secure backend stores, returns, hides from metadata, and deletes one non-biometric QA value.
The route reports its deterministic required case finished with one pass and no failure, while hardware paths remain pending.
features.claimLimit: The marker proves that the required sweep ended; the separate Secure result row carries the operation evidence.
This row records that the default suite omitted hardware cases; it is not a hardware test result.
features.transport: The screen explicitly lists biometric, lock, corruption, and hardware-backed Keychain checks as pending.

features.claimLimit: The summary is limited to the deterministic required case; pending hardware cases do not pass here.
features.transport: The summary counts only the no-prompt required case and explicitly retains a hardware-pending suffix.
The installed example opens the stress route and reports the route ready.
features.claimLimit: The ready row proves only that the Stress screen mounted; it does not prove any write or read succeeded.

features.transport: The bounded Disk and Secure sweep completes before the route marks it finished.
features.claimLimit: The marker proves only that the stress loop ended; the count and detail rows carry operation results.

features.transport: The native Disk and Secure loop counts prove all 40 and 20 values were read back.
The stress screen reports no mismatch detail after all scoped QA keys are removed.
The installed example opens the E2E route through nitrostorage://e2e.
features.claimLimit: The ready row proves only that the E2E route mounted; the separate URL row verifies the displayed deep link.

features.transport: The E2E screen exposes the exact public example deep link.
The seed stage validates the native SQLite Disk capability, writes the exact RUN_ID-scoped value, flushes it, and reads it back.

features.claimLimit: This state confirms only that the seed phase completed; it is not a persistence result.
features.transport: The seed screen remains pending until the app process is relaunched with the same RUN_ID.
The verify stage marks the run finished only after it has read the run value and attempted scoped cleanup.
features.claimLimit: The marker proves only that the verify stage ended; the separate result row proves the value match and cleanup.

features.transport: The verify stage compares the exact RUN_ID-derived value after process relaunch and confirms that its one QA key is deleted.
The native public transaction boundary rejects a Promise result in Memory, Disk, and Secure, restores each original value, and refuses a write through the retained context.
A Disk object item merges a partial value over its default, then setOrDelete(null) removes the stored value.
A typed Memory Set item toggles an existing member off and a new member on, and values() returns the remaining member.
clearGroup removes the two Disk items registered in the e2e-g group and keeps a Disk item outside the group.
A Memory item with a 1 ms TTL is read after a resolved timeout; the read returns the default and fires onExpired and subscribeExpired once each.
Two reserved native Secure keys appear in getAllSecureMetadata and exportSecureUnsafe when filtered by their QA prefix, then are deleted.
The default Secure access control is set to AfterFirstUnlock for a native Secure roundtrip and restored to WhenUnlocked.
A coalesced Secure item returns its queued value before the flush, and the native Secure value exists after flushSecureWrites.
createStorageItem rejects an empty key with the public invalid_key error code.
With a metrics observer installed, getScopedMetricsSnapshot reports setString counters for both the Disk and Secure scopes; the observer and metrics are reset afterwards.

A subscribeKey listener on a reserved Disk key receives the set event for a native Disk write and renders its real change source; the adapter suppresses the native echo of its own write, so the JavaScript emission is the observable event.
A mounted component drives useStorage, useStorageValue, useStorageSelector, useSetStorage, and useStorageActions through set, updater, merge, and remove on a Memory item.
createSecureAuthStorage with a 50 ms TTL in a reserved namespace returns the stored token, then the empty default after the TTL elapses.
The default Secure access control is set to WhenPasscodeSetThisDeviceOnly for one Secure roundtrip and restored to WhenUnlocked; the screen renders the stored result or the public error code.
features.claimLimit: The row proves only that the probe ran and rendered a passcode-acl= result. It does not prove that the item stored (a device without a passcode rejects it) and is a gating probe for Tier 2 iOS biometric work, not a pass.

features.transport: The final suite seeds one reserved key in Memory, Disk, and Secure, calls clearAll, and verifies that each key is absent. It wipes all example storage on the target install.

A Secure createStorageItem with biometric: true and no biometricLevel (the default level) writes a RUN_ID-scoped value without a prompt, and getSecureMetadata reports it as a biometric-protected entry without exposing its value.
features.claimLimit: iOS simulator only. The resolved default biometric level is not publicly observable; metadata proves the biometric representation, not the Keychain access-control flags.

features.transport: The screen renders a prompting token, then item.get() blocks on the Face ID sheet; after `settings faceid match` the public read returns the seeded value.
features.claimLimit: Simulator Face ID via `settings faceid match` after a fixed 1500 ms wait; not hardware Secure Enclave evidence. Nonmatch and cancel outcomes are not asserted.

features.transport: item.delete() and storage.clearBiometric() remove the RUN_ID-scoped biometric item, and getSecureMetadata reads it back as missing without a second prompt.
features.claimLimit: iOS simulator only. Removes the example's biometric Secure items; it does not assert other Secure keys.

pending.reason: The deterministic replay installs and clears the observer but does not force a backend failure. A Secure scheduled-flush failure cannot be forced without a locked or invalidated Keychain/Keystore, so it is infeasible in the default replay. A Disk failure needs a corruption or storage-full fixture and a runner stage that installs it. Controlled unit coverage does not prove native runtime failure delivery.
prerequisites: A controlled native Disk and Secure backend failure that does not exhaust or corrupt device-wide storage
A disposable installed release app with only the replay QA namespace in use
pending.acceptance: On each requested native platform, trigger one scheduled backend failure in the isolated QA scope and assert the callback reports the exact Disk or Secure scope and adapter error once (including its cause when available); record cleanup and recovery evidence.

pending.reason: The iOS simulator Face ID match path is replay-asserted by biometric-ios. Android is not: biometric replay needs fingerprint or PIN enrollment through the device Settings app, which the device rules block. iOS nonmatch and cancel outcomes are not asserted because no `.ad` step dismisses the SpringBoard Face ID sheet, so the blocked read cannot complete. A skipped or unavailable biometric path is not a pass.
prerequisites: Android: a QA emulator or device with fingerprint and PIN enrolled through an authorized path other than the device Settings app
iOS: an `.ad` step or authorized interaction that dismisses the SpringBoard Face ID sheet after a nonmatch or cancel
pending.acceptance: On Android, run the biometric lifecycle flow and verify the public Secure value and prompt outcome. On iOS, assert the documented public error for a nonmatch and a cancel on the RUN_ID-scoped item, then confirm cleanup. Never record credentials.

pending.reason: The default replay does not lock the device, change biometric enrollment, or invalidate a Keychain/Keystore item.
prerequisites: A dedicated QA device and user-approved lock/unlock interaction
A controlled invalidation fixture with a recovery plan for its QA key only
pending.acceptance: Verify locked-state error classification and post-unlock recovery, then separately invalidate the QA item and assert the documented public error without touching unrelated secure keys.

pending.reason: The deterministic replay does not corrupt the native Disk database or delete/recreate persistent app data.
prerequisites: An isolated app installation with a named disposable database fixture
A native corruption trigger that targets only that fixture
pending.acceptance: Run the corruption lifecycle on the isolated fixture, verify the public storage_corruption result across calls, then remove only the named disposable fixture.

pending.reason: The deterministic replay does not fill the device volume or force a native SQLITE_FULL condition.
prerequisites: A disposable native storage volume or controlled backend fault injection
An isolated installed app whose unrelated app data can be preserved
pending.acceptance: Trigger storage_full only in the controlled Disk fixture, assert the public error and subsequent recovery, and preserve unrelated device and app data.

pending.reason: The public capability value does not prove that a device's Keychain or Keystore key is hardware-backed.
prerequisites: A physical device with documented secure hardware capabilities
Platform evidence that identifies the actual key protection level
pending.acceptance: Capture platform-level evidence for the QA key and match it with the public capability and Secure roundtrip result.
